headline: Release courses only after every prerequisite is complete
statement: Given numCourses courses numbered 0..numCourses-1 and prerequisite pairs [course, prerequisite], return any ordering in which every prerequisite appears before its course. Return [] if no such ordering exists.
constraints: Prerequisite pairs are distinct and use valid course numbers
A course is not its own prerequisite
intuition: Build the schedule by repeatedly taking a course with no unfinished prerequisites. After taking it, lower the requirement counts of courses that depend on it. This creates a valid order directly. If the order cannot include every course, a cycle makes a full schedule impossible.
approach: Build edges prerequisite -> course and count each course’s incoming edges.
Queue every course with zero indegree, including isolated courses.
Repeatedly emit a ready course and decrement its dependents’ indegrees.
If fewer than numCourses were emitted, return []; otherwise return the order.
correctness: Every emitted course has no remaining incoming edge, so all its prerequisites were emitted earlier and the prefix is valid. Each removed edge can release its dependent only after all its prerequisites finish. In an acyclic graph some remaining vertex always has indegree zero, so all vertices are emitted. If the queue empties early, the remaining graph contains a cycle and no complete valid order exists.
bruteForce: Try all course permutations and verify every prerequisite position; this can require n! arrangements.

complexity.explanation: V=numCourses and E=prerequisite pairs. Every course and edge is processed once.

pitfalls: The edge direction is prerequisite to course.
A partially valid order is not acceptable when a cycle blocks the rest.
